trust_decision.summary: The multipart body processor decides which filename a file-upload part carries (and whether the part is a file at all) for FILES/FILES_SIZES rules, taking only mime.ParseMediaType's params["filename"], which silently ignores filename* under charsets other than utf-8/us-ascii.

landing_point.why: originFileName is the only code that reads the Content-Disposition filename; the summary names multipart filename* and FILES, which leads straight here.

fix_sites.entry_point: Transaction.ProcessRequestBody with Content-Type multipart/form-data (internal/corazawaf/transaction.go:392-393, 1138) or ctl:requestBodyProcessor=MULTIPART (internal/actions/ctl.go:253-255)
fix_sites.module_kind: core parser (originFileName rewritten: independent filename*/filename scanner, continuation and quoting handling)
core body processor loop (file-vs-field classification, MULTIPART_FILENAME/NAME population, strict-error flags)
core body processor (second FILES/FILES_SIZES entry for the alternate reading)
public interface plumbing for new variables

fix_sites.entry_point: Transaction.Collection / Variables() used by rule evaluation

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Only one multipart filename extractor exists at the pinned commit (internal/bodyprocessors/multipart.go:140-148); other changed files are variable plumbing, not a second route to the flaw.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 name* route: the advisory is about filename*, RFC 7578 says field names use percent-encoding rather than RFC 5987, and the part name feeds argument names rather than FILES, so it looks like a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A plain-filename upload, a utf-8 filename*, and a part that has only filename* must still be classified as a file (FILES, FILES_SIZES, FILES_COMBINED_SIZE); parts without a filename must stay in ARGS_POST. A fix that rejects every non-utf-8 charset, or every filename/filename* mismatch, breaks legitimate RFC 5987 uploads. A fix that ignores filename* sends filename*-only parts to ARGS_POST.

O7_producer.where: The value comes from Go stdlib mime.ParseMediaType (decode2231Enc), called directly in internal/bodyprocessors/multipart.go:142; there is no project-level schema, serializer or cache.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Part field name comes from p.FormName() (stdlib ParseMediaType params["name"]), so a name* extended parameter under a non-utf-8 charset is dropped the same way. That name feeds FILES_NAMES, ARGS_POST keys and MULTIPART_PART_HEADERS keys, and the fix did not change it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory concerns filename* and FILES; field names are a different parameter, RFC 7578 does not endorse name*, and it is unclear whether common backends honour name*.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and function as the fix (internal/bodyprocessors/multipart.go:101, 117)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: FILES_NAMES derived from p.FormName() could get its own name*-aware extractor that misses the non-utf-8 charset case, mirroring the filename bug.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding RFC 5987 support for field names would naturally reuse the stdlib, which carries the same utf-8/us-ascii-only restriction.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An audit-log Part J or upload-hook path that re-reads the part's filename from the raw header instead of FILES.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Part J mirrors ModSecurity's format and could plausibly be fed by a second, simpler filename parse; today it consumes FILES via internal/corazawaf/transaction.go:1657-1661.

O9_family: parser differential / interpretation conflict (CWE-436) in WAF multipart filename extraction, leading to a rule bypass
